label_agreement.method: blinded second reader (a separate AI subagent) labelled the same 20 from the title and the prior-item list only, without the first reader's labels; the first reader's Maia labels were written after the blind result was available, so for this corpus only the second reader is blind
label_agreement.note: label stability of one reader, not correctness; the labels and the sample are published

known_prior_recall.reason: fewer than 5 defensible known-prior positives exist in this corpus; the value is reported with its n but is not a rate (see BENCHMARK.md dead ends)

duplicate_recall.note: supplementary judged-duplicate retrieval, not the plan's known-issue metric

release.status: the measured binary is a local release-profile build; record the published release binary hash and tag here when this corpus's measurement is tied to a release

not_claimed: not a measurement of whether priorart finds bugs: the corpus is judged human findings
not a false-positive rate on model-written hypotheses
not a duplicate-detector score for submissions against public reports: the duplicate variant is a reading list and never a duplicate verdict
the known-prior positives are one reader's grounding, not the judge's published reason
the corpus is smaller than the Tapioca corpus (9 audit prior items), so the false-alarm denominator is not comparable across the two corpora
the first measured run opened this corpus's frozen held-out split; the number is out-of-sample with respect to matcher development, but no held-out remainder is left
